text:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up: proposal for "hole-preservation" flag vs eager coalesce. We observed spiky reuse patterns; maybe we should avoid immediately coalescing tiny adjacent holes to keep LRU locality. Short thread to capture tradeoffs.

vik: tl;dr: keep small holes around for a short TTL to service micro-alloc bursts?

anya: Yes. Concrete: when spans are freed after host-return, mark as HOLE_PRESERVE with expiry = now + preserve_ms. Allocation prefers preserved holes in same pool/tenant before splitting big free spans or spilling to host. After expiry, normal coalesce runs.

oscar: Risk: preserved holes increase fragmentation and may block large allocations. How to mitigate?

anya: Limits: max_preserve_bytes per-pool and per-tenant; global backpressure if allocation failures increase, decay preserve_ms. Also preserved holes are size-bucketed, we avoid preserving > 64KB by default.

mei: Implementation complexity: need a new list and cheap check on alloc hot path. We can add a bitmap in span header "P" bit set on free and index by sizeclass.

oscar: Telemetry: preserved_count, preserve_hits, preserve_evictions, preserve_blocked_allocs.

allocator-bot: scheduled preserve-gc sweep in 2m for gpu-0 :gear: 

vik: Concern: multi-tenant fairness: a noisy tenant could capture preserved holes and starve others. Make preserve per-tenant or tag preserved spans with tenant id.

anya: Agreed. Preserve reservoirs are tenant-scoped when tenant metadata exists; otherwise per-pool. Default OFF for Dedicated.

mei: Also think about interaction with background compacting: compact should ignore preserved holes until expiry. That reduces lock thrash.

oscar: Sounds plausible. Add stress tests: bursty micro-alloc workload with interleaved large allocs to ensure no regressions.

anya: I'll draft follow-up PR with API sketches, telemetry, knobs, and a small perf harness. Any objections?

vik: :thumbsup: no objections.

oscar: +1

mei: +1, include opt-out flag and default conservative limits.

anya: will share RFC link once draft is up.
